_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The Markdown file editor leaves shortcuts to the stacked command palette. The conversation /c/{{SLUG}} runs in a directory holding notes.md, which reads "# A note". To "open F": press "p" (lowercase) with the Control modifier (on whatever has focus); wait for the finder input ".grp-filter" to be visible; fill it with F; wait for the FIRST ".grp-row" to contain F (assert_text_contains on ".grp-row", which checks the first match: the finder lists every file until the query applies, and Enter opens the top row, so waiting for any row with the text is not enough); press Enter in the finder input; the dialog (role "dialog") whose accessible name matches the regular expression /Edit .*F/ is then "the modal" for F, and its ".monaco-editor" should become visible (up to 15s). "The preview" is the modal's region (role "region") named "Markdown preview". "The editor input" is the modal's ".monaco-editor textarea.inputarea"; to focus it, eval its focus(). Key presses go to whatever has focus; do not click anything to focus first unless a step says so. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. 2. Open notes.md. 3. Click the modal's button named "Preview mode". 4. Press "k" with the Control modifier. 5. The command palette's input ".command-palette-input" should become focused (document.activeElement is it; the palette focuses its input a task after it opens, and until then the shortcut is still the editor's). 6. Press "p" (lowercase) with the modifiers Control+Alt. 7. The preview should still be visible. 8. ".command-palette-input" should still be focused.
